name: ANSI/IEEE pressure/current converter symbol
aliases: IEEE pressure to current converter symbol
summary: IEEE-library pressure-to-current converter form representing a transducer that turns process pressure into a loop current.
description: The pressure/current converter represents a transducer that measures pressure and produces a proportional electrical signal, typically a 4-20 mA loop. On control and protection schematics it appears where transformer, compressor or hydraulic pressure is passed to a PLC, relay or indicator.

The block does not tell you the pressure range, whether the output is two-wire loop-powered or four-wire, or whether the measurement is gauge, absolute or differential. Those details govern the wiring and the scaling at the receiving input.
readingNotes: Identify whether the loop is powered by the receiver or the transducer.
Check scaling of the output current to pressure range.
distinction: A pressure/current converter gives a continuous signal; a pressure switch gives only a contact change at a set point.
